assertions: Essex will take Reading — the town will fall into the hands of Parliament's army under Essex
The town will not be carried by a direct storm or assault, but will be delivered up / surrendered on terms by composition rather than taken by the sword and sacked
The governor of the town, signified by Saturn lord of the 4th in his fall, is weak, untenable and afflicted, and will be compelled to yield, with loss of honour in the surrender
The King's party in the town, signified by the Sun in the 7th in a fixed sign, will hold out obstinately for a time, so the taking is not instantaneous

The town's ammunition and provisions are not presently exhausted — Jupiter lord of the 5th and Venus placed therein are well placed for the town's stores — so surrender is not caused primarily by immediate lack of munitions or victuals
The matter is perfected in the course of the present siege in April, with delivery of the town in late April, on the timescale of 27 April given in the siege chronology

Essex himself, Mars lord of the Scorpio Ascendant, is well fortified apart from being in his fall and is in reception with the Moon in the 10th near Regulus, so he prevails and gains honour from the outcome despite his army's debility
method: Lilly horary, Christian Astrology Book II siege rules — classical dignities, reception and application, whole-sign significators
reasoning: Asc lord Mars (Essex) is essentially well fortified apart from his fall and in mutual reception with the Moon (Mars in the Moon's house, Moon in his terms/face, in 10th near Regulus); Moon void of course argues nothing by direct force, then applying to Mars (sextile counted as a square in signs of long ascension) perfects the matter with difficulty and by delivery rather than storm. Saturn, lord of Aquarius 4th for the town and its governor, is in his fall — the besieged commander is weak and must yield. Sun, the King's significator, in the 7th in a fixed sign shows obstinate resistance first. Jupiter lord of the 5th and Venus in the 5th show the town's ammunition and provision still in good condition, so the cause of yielding is the governor's untenable position, not immediate starvation.
summary: Essex will take Reading, not by storm but by the governor's surrender/delivery of the town on terms in late April.
